comparator.name: Archaeology
comparator.sourceNotes: Permitted separate revisit on 13 November 2026. Current programme and 28 module API responses were retrieved successfully with 12 November imports. All 19 first-year entries were reconciled: twelve 5-EC parents total 60 EC, six World Archaeology subunits carry 0 EC and Active Bystander training carries 0 EC. Current Field School admission still requires passed Field Techniques and Natural Landscapes and attended Active Bystander training; its practical and reports are assessed. Field Techniques practical attendance is compulsory. Current catalogue text supports genuine 30-EC minor, exchange or coherent elective space, with applicable approval, non-overlap and level conditions; self-composed 30-EC study requires at least 10 EC at level 300 or above. The verified partial record remains 90 EC. The current annual API still combines common year-2 study of 20 EC with two 40-EC WA/HS groups; year 3 lists common 30 EC and outside-study 30 EC. This does not explicitly establish the September 2026 general entrant allocation. Independently inspected annual later-year entries have a 10-EC thesis requiring Designing Archaeological Research and a 5-EC internship requiring Field School; those annual facts are retained as research, not silently certified as the new cohort pathway. Current Dutch and English programme pages describe later themes, internships and elective possibilities without supplying an explicit cohort correspondence. Prior verified 2026–2027 OER findings remain preserved: Article 2.2 restricts WA/HS specialisations to earlier entrants, Article 2.9 defines the language versions, Article 3.1 specifies compulsory study and delegates structure to the prospectus, and thesis/practical/progression details are delegated. The previously verified September replacement table changes three first-year codes rather than establishing the later-year allocation. Direct HTTP requests to the programme and PDF URLs now return Access Blocked HTML; HTTP 200 is not accepted as substantive content. Actual programme-page content was inspectable through web retrieval, but this pass did not retrieve the current OER or replacement PDF through either route and does not claim fresh identical PDF bytes or freshly reverified formal clauses. Historical source hashes and findings remain historical. The selected public source is the exact Dutch-offering programme overview, whose actual content was inspected; the formal and transition URLs remain additional sources. The remaining compulsory 90-EC allocation, bounded choices and applicable internship/thesis/progression framework remain unresolved. No outgoing route, future delivery or UCR no-match is inferred.

exception.reason: The inspected current material does not establish the complete curriculum for students starting the general Archaeology programme in September 2026. The first-year 60 EC and 30 EC of elective space are supported. The remaining compulsory 90 EC need applicable course and choice, internship and thesis allocation rules or an explicit cohort correspondence. Current later-year catalogue groups retain the earlier specialisation structure. Current regulation and transition PDF content could not be retrieved in this pass; earlier verified formal findings are preserved without claiming a fresh PDF verification.
exception.curriculumContext: Supported partial curriculum: twelve 5-EC first-year parent units total 60 EC, plus 30 EC of genuine approved elective space, giving 90 EC. Six zero-credit World Archaeology subunits and Active Bystander training add no credits. Field School requires passed Field Techniques and Natural Landscapes and attendance at Active Bystander training. No outgoing WA/HS formal route is adopted for the general new entrant. Later annual catalogue course facts, UCR concepts, schedules and alignments remain research rather than a certified complete comparison.

audience.programmeDescription: Archaeology at Leiden studies past societies through material remains, landscapes and heritage. It combines historical interpretation, scientific and digital analysis, artefact studies and practical fieldwork. Students entering from September 2026 follow a general programme without formal specialisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because the published material does not establish the full curriculum for the new entrant cohort. The supported components are shown below. UCR offers relevant archaeology, heritage and research courses; the curriculum gap is not a conclusion that no suitable UCR response exists.

curriculum.limitation: This list contains 90 EC: the first-year 60 EC and 30 EC of approved elective space. The remaining compulsory 90 EC, including later course choices, internship and thesis allocation, still require cohort-specific clarification. It is not a complete 180-EC degree pathway.

componentNotes.arch1-06: Field Techniques includes mandatory practical attendance and archaeological recording exercises.
componentNotes.arch1-12: Field School requires passed Field Techniques and Natural Landscapes and attendance at the additional zero-credit Active Bystander training. The field practical and reports are assessed.
componentNotes.arch-open-30: 30 EC of recognised minor, exchange or approved elective study, without overlap with compulsory courses. A self-composed package needs coherence and at least 10 EC at level 300 or higher. Exchange requires a passed first year, a complementary programme and no study delay; applicable approval conditions apply.
